requirement: Describe a 12-month diabetes coaching study whose randomized comparison is technology-enhanced peer coaching versus peer support alone, with baseline, 6-month, and 12-month assessments; keep the separate usual-care cohort explicitly observational.

evidence.text: The protocol defines the intervention comparison, observed usual-care group, and assessment times.
The DAP separates the randomized arms from the observed usual-care comparison.

requirement: Define the primary endpoint as change in HbA1c from baseline to 6 months for TEC versus peer support alone.

evidence.text: Aim 1 specifies A1c measurement and the TEC versus peer-support contrast.
The primary endpoint is explicitly baseline-to-6-month mean HbA1c change.

requirement: Analyze systolic blood pressure, medication adherence, satisfaction and involvement with care, social support, diabetes-specific distress or quality of life, and related patient-centered outcomes as secondary endpoints.

evidence.text: Aims 2 and 3 enumerate clinical, adherence, and patient-centered measures.
The DAP maps these outcomes to mixed models or GEE.

requirement: Plan 348 randomized patients, 174 per arm, and 87 peer mentors so that 148 patients per arm remain after up to 15% attrition; base power on a 0.5 percentage-point HbA1c difference, SD 1.45, two-sided alpha 0.05, 80% power, and within-pair ICC 0.03.

evidence.text: The DAP provides the complete clustered sample-size calculation.

requirement: Use an intention-to-treat principle for the randomized TEC comparison: analyze patients according to their initial pairing and randomized arm even after dropout or peer-coach reassignment.

evidence.text: The DAP specifies analysis according to initial pairing in an ITT analysis.

requirement: Analyze 6-month HbA1c change with a general linear mixed regression that includes randomized intervention as a fixed effect and peer-coach pair as a random effect to account for within-dyad correlation.

evidence.text: The DAP specifies the primary mixed model and pairing random effect.

requirement: Report unadjusted effects, then use mixed-model ANCOVA to adjust only for clinically important baseline imbalances; report adjusted and unadjusted arm means with 95% confidence intervals.

evidence.text: The analysis sequence and reporting requirements are prespecified.

requirement: Assess sustainability of HbA1c effects through 12 months using repeated-measures mixed-model ANCOVA.

evidence.text: The DAP identifies a repeated-measures ANCOVA for baseline-to-12-month effects.

requirement: Do not treat the observed usual-care cohort as randomized; compare it with peer support using the same broad modeling approach but adjust at least for baseline HbA1c, age, sex, and race and inspect further prognostic imbalances.

evidence.text: The protocol calls usual care an observed group.
The DAP prespecifies covariate adjustment for this nonrandomized comparison.

requirement: Use mixed-effects models for continuous secondary outcomes and GEE with clustering for ordinal outcomes.

evidence.text: The DAP specifies outcome-type-specific model families.

requirement: For engagement, mediation, and moderation, use nested multivariable models or path analysis, center moderators before interaction tests, and interpret significant interactions graphically.

evidence.text: The protocol defines engagement, mediator, and moderator measures.
The DAP defines the nested and interaction analyses.

requirement: Perform an observed-data analysis plus propensity-stratified random-draw imputation for missing outcomes; compare arm dropout rates and completers with noncompleters, use scale-recommended item imputation, and repeat HbA1c analysis assuming no improvement among incomplete cases.

evidence.text: The missing-data section gives all components of the planned analyses.

requirement: Summarize adverse symptoms, including hypoglycemic symptoms or episodes, by randomized group and assessment period.

evidence.text: The protocol specifies collection of adverse symptoms and hypoglycemia.

requirement: Confirm whether the many secondary, mediator, moderator, and usual-care comparisons are exploratory or require a multiplicity strategy; do not imply familywise control from nominal alpha 0.05.

evidence.text: The protocol defines numerous analyses without a familywise testing hierarchy.
The DAP does not state a multiplicity adjustment.

requirement: Ask the statistical team to confirm the randomization unit and blocking or stratification, exact analysis-set exclusions, covariance and degrees-of-freedom choices, the current relevance of the planned 348-patient target, and executable missing-data imputation details.

evidence.text: The concise protocol does not fully operationalize these decisions.
The DAP supplies some but not all implementation details.

notes: Registry final enrollment is an observed result and must not replace the protocol target.
